data.narrative:
Cambridge Aerospace, a Series B defense and security company founded by Steven Barrett and Chris Sylvan, has raised $300M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 peers—2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private Series B-stage firms in Defense & Security, including Dream Security, Allen Control Systems, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, and Twenty.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy base of $300M and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yields $570M. Peer-median analysis across the 8 private comparables shows a median valuation of $1.1B, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The peer set reflects material dispersion, likely driven by differences in revenue trajectory, technology maturity, and customer concentration within the defense sector.

Synthesizing these methods produces a triangulated range of $484M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $848M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer multiples support valuations toward the upper range. Key uncertainties include the company's revenue base and growth rate relative to peers, contract backlog visibility, and customer concentration risk—factors that explain the wide dispersion observed in the comparable set and constrain precision within this range.
